name: Amos Davies
role: Commerce merchant told to invest in the Nauvoo House
dateNote: He was baptized in April 1840; section 124 names him in January 1841.
importance: He was a merchant and postmaster at Commerce before the Saints arrived. Section 124 tells him to pay stock to those building the Nauvoo House. It says he must also obey Joseph Smith’s counsel and be humble. In 1842–1843 the city of Nauvoo brought several cases against him, including slander of Joseph Smith.
connections: He dealt with Joseph Smith and the Nauvoo House committee of George Miller, Lyman Wight, John Snider, and Peter Haws.

sources.title: Amos Davis, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP (spelled Amos Davis): born c. 20 Sept. 1813, New Hampshire or Vermont; Commerce c. 1836; postmaster 1839; baptized Apr. 1840; Nauvoo Legion captain 1841; city cases for slander, assault, and selling liquor 1842–1843; died 22 Mar. 1872, Hancock County, Illinois. The details of 124:112–114 were read in the local text.
